@@ -0,0 +1,86 @@
+# Fused DeepSeek-V3 router override
+
+The router override preserves native checkpoint parameters and distributed
+ownership while specializing routing pointwise work and its backward. The
+gate stays an ordinary BF16 linear; sequence auxiliary loss remains external.
+
+## Authorship
+
+Original implementation and tests: Yidi Wu (@ydwu4),
+[#5258](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/5258), source revision
+`a5d8990c5e9b46e3a87007b33de8e03c09fb97b7`. Copyright/license are preserved.
+This integration adapts BF16 storage and per-branch gradient rounding, padding,
+explicit round-robin benchmark routing, current model/metric APIs and required
+dispatch checks. General-shape kernels and native reduction-order handling
+are additional work in this PR. It is not an unmodified kernel or a wrapper-only port.
+
+## Shape and launch contract
+
+The fused API accepts nonempty CUDA BF16/FP32 logits `[T,E]`, valid top-k and
+group counts, with optional bias and padding. Token counts, expert counts and
+top-k are compile-time launch parameters, not a public benchmark-shape allowlist.
+FP32 score/group arithmetic, normalization and native unsorted expert order
+are preserved. Gradient reductions retain ATen's row/column-major accumulator
+and warp order, including unaligned vector tails.
+
+```text
+native gate -> logits[T,E]
+                    |
+             fused operator
+             /            \
+ tuned 671B geometry       other legal geometries
+ preserved CuTe kernel    parameterized Triton kernel
+             \            /
+      weights[T,K], IDs[T,K], map[T,E], counts[E], scores[T,E]
+                    |
+       two score-gradient branches -> native gate backward
+```
+
+The general forward zeros fresh integer counts and fuses sigmoid, group/top-k
+selection, routing weights, the map and exact integer usage accumulation.
+Its saved state is scores, selected values/IDs and one denominator per row.
+Calls at different shapes do not share a shape-dependent arrival-counter budget.
+The tuned CuTe path retains its existing stream-ordered counter and layouts.
+Hardware-specific launch variants do not replace general fusion with eager code.
+
+## Precision and execution
+
+```text
+BF16 hidden + BF16 gathered gate weight
+                    |
+             native BF16 GEMM
+                    |
+               BF16 logits
+                    |
+       fused FP32 sigmoid / group top-k
+                    |
+          +---------+------------+
+          |                      |
+ BF16 selected weights    FP32 unbiased scores
+          |                      |
+   routed expert path      external aux loss
+          |                      |
+ FP32 route derivative    FP32 aux derivative
+          |                      |
+     round BF16             round BF16
+          +----------+-----------+
+                     |
+           BF16 gradient accumulation
+                     |
+          native gate DGRAD / WGRAD
+```
+
+The 671B learned recipe uses256 experts, top8, eight groups/four selected groups,

**Claude finished @tianyu-l's task in 4m 52s** —— [View job](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/actions/runs/41279171983)

---
**Request changes.** Under the MLPerf recipe, the fused router's BF16 backward produces different gradients from the native router, and the production GB300 CuTe kernel never runs in CI. Details are in 7 inline comments.

<details><summary>Review summary</summary>

### Blocking
1. **The override changes numerics** (`fused_dsv3_router.py:324-333`). The recipe uses a BF16 `Linear` gate, `Sigmoid(fp32)` and `routing_weight_dtype=bf16`. In that configuration the native router sums the route and aux gradients into the same `scores_TE` in FP32 and rounds to BF16 once. `_AuxLossInjection` stays in the same autograd graph, so this is how native works today. The fused kernel instead rounds each branch to BF16 separately and uses a different sigmoid-backward op order.
   - Enabling the override therefore changes training gradients.
   - The native fallback path still gives native numerics, so results depend on which path a call takes.
   - Either match native, or make the NVIDIA-style rounding an explicit choice and include a loss comparison against the unfused recipe (CLAUDE.md "Show numerical proof").
2. **Test gaps** (`tests/unit_tests/gpu/test_fused_dsv3_router.py:225`).
   - The CuTe class only runs on SM 10.3; B200 CI is SM 10.0. About 800 lines of inline PTX, DSMEM code and the arrival-counter protocol are never tested continuously, and that is the path production runs use.
   - Every module-level comparison uses a `HiMidLoLinear` gate (FP32 logits). None covers the recipe's BF16 `Linear` setup against the native `DeepSeekV3Router`.
   - Consider landing the Triton path first and the CuTe specialization separately, with a measured end-to-end gain. The current evidence is "prior qualified microbenchmarks".

### Should fix
3. **Recompiles:** `TOKENS` is a `tl.constexpr` in both Triton kernels, so each distinct token count triggers a new JIT compile. Pass bucketed values computed on the host instead (`:168`).
4. **Forward/backward dispatch can disagree.**
   - The backward doesn't check the multiprocessor count, groups or epsilon that the forward checks, so one call can mix the two backends.
   - The CuTe backward flushes subnormals to zero when not deterministic; the Triton backward never does.
   - Decide the backend once in the forward and store it on `ctx` (`:1416`).
